==== Verification process
Verification process 
 Our payment processor, Stripe, requires additional information to verify the identity of the account holder after a certain amount of time has passed and sales accrued. This is a standard practice in the financial industry and is part of their Know Your Customer (KYC) obligations . 
 Note: In rare cases, Stripe makes a final decision to reject an account. If that happens, we email you once to let you know, verification requests stop, and any remaining balance of $1 or more is paid out automatically even if it is below the usual $100 minimum, unless we are separately holding your balance for another reason, such as an open review of your account, suspected fraud, or misleading or deceptive marketing, in which case it stays held until that is resolved. Your payments settings page shows your account status. See this article for details. 
 ID verification 
 You can learn the correct documents needed for ID verification for your specific location here . 
 Before you upload your ID 
 
 Use a color photo or scan. You can take it with a phone, webcam, or scanner. 
 For a driver's license or identity card, upload images of both the front and back of the ID. 
 Use a JPEG or PNG file. 
 Do not upload a PDF. 
 
 Address verification 
 You can learn the correct documents needed for address verification for your specific location here . 
 If your registered address is a P.O. Box: Stripe does not accept a P.O. Box as the address on the account, so your payout settings have to carry a different address. If the only address printed on your documents is that P.O. Box, the document will keep being rejected for not matching the account, and uploading it again will not change the outcome. Email support@gumroad.com and we will work out with you which address and document can be used. 
 Social Security number (SSN) 
 SSN is required for US sellers. The name and date of birth on your SSN must match exactly with the information filled in your Payments Settings . Refer to your social security card to see how your name is formatted, and enter your name in the settings exactly as it is on the card. If you have a middle name, you can add it to the First Name field on the settings page. 
 
 If you don't have your Social Security card, or if you believe you've entered the correct information but still receive an error, please contact the Social Security Administration. You can request a copy of your card or update your name here: https://www.ssa.
==== The account review process
The account review process 
 
 Payout modes 
 
 Note: How your buyers pay you and how you get paid out are two separate things. Gumroad accepts many payment methods at checkout, including cards, PayPal, and local methods such as UPI in India, and which ones a buyer sees depends on where the buyer is. Your payout is not affected by any of that. In general, sales land in your Gumroad balance and are then paid out to you the one way you have set up below, in your own payout currency. The exception is PayPal sales when you have connected your own PayPal account , which are credited to you at the time of sale instead. 
 
 We support direct bank deposits in the local currency for most countries. For countries where bank deposits are not available, we offer PayPal transfers as the only payment option. 
 We do not support alternative payout modes like Payoneer, Wise, check, money order, wire transfer, etc. If your country is not supported by direct bank deposits or PayPal, then unfortunately, we have no way to pay you out for now. 
 To get paid for your sales, start by filling out your Payments Settings . 
 Get paid to your bank account 
 
 Note: Unpaid amounts on a country-specific connected account cannot move to a new country's account, so changing payout country (or switching payout method in a way that needs a new connected account) forfeits those amounts. Amounts in Gumroad's own payment accounts are not forfeited. If we can transfer the money, we will. The confirmation names the amount and asks you to type "I understand". Wait for any payout in progress to finish first. See Section 11.4 of the Terms of Service.
